question: Does isolation-generated visitor scarcity change the marginal return to investment at identical plant phenotype and selfing capacity?
plants: Matched intervention founders:48 plants; identical matching/investment variation, all capacity0.5; no population updates.
capacity: fixed0.5 in both configurations; no demographic replicates because assay is deterministic
gradient: Existing investment_assay: perturb one focal plant, measure .5 maternal outcross +.5 paternal outcross + viable selfed offspring; all other plants fixed.
precision_gate: Every focal gradient differs by at most1e-4+1e-3*abs(fine gradient); retain failures, no ecological readout if any fail.
pollen: Natural receipt and existing raw/viable saturation deficits on same plants.
outputs: history-level mean gradient and fraction negative
all individual gradients and step differences
analysis: Paired far-minus-near history differences;5000 descriptive history bootstrap draws; no multiplicity correction. Negative gradient denotes local reduction favoured in this contribution assay, not proven realized evolutionary response.
limits: Changes arise from visitor identities/counts together, not a richness-only manipulation. Single fixed capacity; timing and cost jointly differ. No infinite-population rare-mutant inference and no causal mediation percentage. Do not equate total contribution derivative with a separately measured physiological cost term.
